主要内容: Ulta Beauty shares fell more than 8% after the company reported weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results, citing a decline in cosmetics sales during the pandemic. CEO Mary Dillon will step down in June and be replaced by President Dave Kimbell. Kecia Steelman, Ulta's chief store operations officer, will be promoted to chief operating officer. The company reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income of $171.5 million, or $3.03 per share, compared with $222.7 million, or $3.89 per share, a year earlier. Excluding items, Ulta earned $3.41 per share, topping the $2.35 per share expected by analysts. Net sales fell to $2.2 billion from $2.31 billion a year ago, beating expectations of $2.08 billion. For fiscal 2021, Ulta expects to earn between $8.85 and $9.30 per share on revenue of $7.2 billion to $7.3 billion. Analysts had been expecting Ulta to earn $10.61 per share on revenue of $7.32 billion. Same-store sales are expected to be in the range of 15% to 17%. Ulta plans to open 40 net new stores and remodel about 21 stores in the coming year. Due to the pandemic stretching on and the slow vaccine rollout, Ulta executives do not expect a strong recovery this year. Ulta Beauty shares fell after the company issued a weaker-than-expected outlook, citing ongoing challenges from masking requirements and social distancing. Ulta's CFO, Scott Settersten, noted that while makeup sales declined due to more people staying home, the company remains optimistic about the long-term prospects of the beauty category. Dave Kimbell, the new CEO, emphasized that customer engagement with makeup, fashion, and styles will continue to evolve. Ulta has been affected by temporary store closures during the pandemic, but after reopening stores in July, the company saw a strong comeback in its mobile app and e-commerce platforms. In November, Ulta announced plans to open small cosmetic shops within Target stores to boost sales and expand its reach. The company's performance reflects broader challenges in the retail sector amid ongoing health restrictions.
